Subject: Questions on DPA addendum for split-region routing

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re progressing through legal and our security review; there are two items they flagged that I wanted to surface before we move to signatures:

1) We need an explicit DPA addendum that documents conditional split-region routing (US/EU primary; APAC only as transient failover for 72h in outage scenarios). Legal wants the tolerance window and the gating conditions spelled out.

2) Subprocessor visibility during temporary APAC syncs — can you confirm the roster and whether there’s an automated notice when a transient hop occurs? Our SOC team also asked about KMS separation (can keys remain in-region or must they be escrowed?).

I attached a short doc with the redline questions and suggested wording (MedSpect_DPA_questions.docx).

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can:
- Commit to a 72-hour maximum transient window (and whether logs/notifications will be available in near-real-time)
- Provide a subprocessor gating step (i.e., ops-only initiated failover with an audit log TTL)

If useful, I can set up a short call with our DPO tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Emma Park
Head of Security & Privacy

Folks —

Quick technical clarifications to feed into the addendum draft:

1) Transient APAC window: our platform supports an operator-initiated failover that can span up to 72 hours. We classify this as an emergency routing event (rare, manual trigger) and it is distinct from regular regional autoscaling.

2) Telemetry & logs:
- Audit entries are produced immediately on the routing decision and include: timestamp, triggering condition (region outage/ASG drain), operator id, model variant used, and the target region.
- Log push cadence to our compliance stream is configurable; standard retention for transient-hop audit events is 365 days. We can add a per-customer SLA to surface these entries to an S3 bucket or a secure Drive within 2 hours of the event.

3) KMS and key residency:
- For the failover window, we can operate with region-scoped keys if the customer's KMS supports cross-region tokenized unwrap (most cloud KMSs support this). If MedSpect requires absolute in-region key material during the failover we’d need a key-escrow addendum and a brief ops playbook — we can document that as an optional clause.

4) Subprocessor gating & roster:
- Ops-initiated failovers will spin up instances that use our standard inference stack; subprocessors (cloud provider compute, telemetry pipeline) are the same as normal. We can attach a transient-hop subprocessor roster and add a notification webhook to MedSpect’s security endpoint when a failover occurs.
- Attached: subprocessor_roster_20280625.csv (names and cloud regions).

Proposed language to include in addendum: a) explicit definition of an "emergency transient hop" (trigger list), b) 72-hour cap, c) notification SLA (2 hours), d) audit retention 365d, e) optional KMS escrow clause.

Happy to sync on a quick call to finalize the redline.

—Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: subprocessor_roster_20280625.csv (csv)]

Subject: DPA addendum redline and next steps

Emma —

Thanks — we discussed offline and Karthik’s language addresses the key asks. Attached is our proposed redline (redline_DPA_addendum_20280627.pdf) that:

- Defines "Emergency transient hop" and lists triggering conditions (region outage, cumulative AZ failure > 50% of capacity, customer-authorized evacuation)
- Commits to a 72-hour maximum transient processing window and a 2-hour notification SLA to the customer security webhook
- Includes audit log retention of 365 days and the option for push to a customer-controlled S3 bucket
- Offers an optional KMS escrow clause if MedSpect requires strict in-region key material during the failover
- Attaches the transient-hop subprocessor roster and describes the notification webhook payload (timestamp, operator id, region, runbook id)

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the correct signer on MedSpect’s side (legal or DPO) — Jordan, if you want me to route to procurement/legal let me know.
2) If MedSpect wants the KMS escrow clause, we’ll add a short appendix and schedule a 30-min ops walkthrough (Karthik + MedSpect infra).
3) We’ll aim to get DocuSign out within 48 hours once you confirm the signer.

Emma — happy to take the call if your DPO wants to walk through the failure triggers and webhook sample payload.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
